clue.text: Vegetables I stuffed into metal container that doesn't close

indicators.note: stuffed into says the single letter is packed inside the metal-plus-container string

parts.note: brass is a metal alloy of copper and zinc

indicators.note: a container that doesn't close lacks its closing letter, so the word loses its end

parts.note: a case is a container

explanation.surface: Someone crams greens into a metal tin whose lid won't shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal container' wants to be a single object such as a tin; the metal and the container are separate pieces, and 'that doesn't close' drops the container word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassicas are the cabbage family of plants, eaten as greens such as cabbage, sprouts and turnips.

clue.text: Dull British countryside

parts.note: land is the countryside, rural terrain

explanation.surface: Britain's rural landscape is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means dull, lacking flavour or interest.

clue.text: Fire a colleague, bringing new one in

indicators.note: bringing, with in after the pieces, says the letters are brought into the middle
in marks where the new letters go, inside the a-and-colleague string

parts.note: a mate is a colleague
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sacks a co-worker and hires a replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like 'sack', which suits the surface, but means to stir up; N and I go between A and MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone with enthusiasm is to animate them, enliven them.

clue.text: Clergyman's estate in foreign province provides somewhere to sleep

indicators.note: in says the estate word sits inside the province word

parts.note: Sind is a province of Pakistan
a glebe is land belonging to a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar's land in an overseas province offers a place to stay the night.
explanation.walkthrough: A glebe was the farmland that came with a Church of England parish to support its priest; Sind is in Pakistan. The surface's bed-and-breakfast picture hides that 'in' is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A single bed is a bed for one person, somewhere to sleep.

clue.text: Secret agent sent out where the action is

indicators.note: sent out says the letters are dispatched and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy is dispatched to the scene of the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Centre stage is the middle of the stage where the main drama happens, figuratively the focus of events.

clue.text: Dishonest scheme hasn't caught him?

indicators.note: hasn't says the scheme word goes without the letter for caught

parts.note: a scam is a dishonest scheme
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A con trick fails to net its target.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'him?', a man's name given by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam is a man's name, so it is one possible person meant by the pronoun.

clue.text: Maybe watch broadcast about middle of afternoon

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for broadcast is read backwards

parts.note: to broadcast is to emit a signal

indicators.note: the middle of the nine-letter word afternoon is its fifth letter

explanation.surface: Someone's watch is transmitting something halfway through the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EMIT into TIME; the middle letter of 'afternoon' is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a timing device, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Several men following course

indicators.note: following says the soldiers word comes after the number word

parts.note: ten is several, a number
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A handful of men follow a route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following course' looks like a phrase for taking a route, but 'following' joins the pieces and 'course' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of something is its general course or drift.

clue.text: Manchester United's outside right, number one scorer

indicators.note: outside says the club's nickname goes around the other letters

parts.note: Man U is the common nickname for Manchester United football club
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A football club's outside-right winger is its top goal scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside right' is a football position, a misdirection; RT and I go inside MAN U. The 'scorer' is a composer of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohuslav Martinu was a Czech composer, and a scorer writes musical scores.

clue.text: Journalist going after position in bank, according to general belief

indicators.note: in says the position-and-journalist string sits inside the bank word

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: going after says the journalist comes after the position word

parts.note: to put is to position
ED, editor, is a usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter follows up a job at a bank, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb here: to bank on something is to RELY on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputedly means as commonly said or believed.

clue.text: A Cotes-du-Rhone -—— good little number — cellared here?

indicators.note: cellared, stored away like wine below ground, puts letters inside the wine word

parts.note: a Cotes-du-Rhone is a French wine, vin in French
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A wine connoisseur wonders whether a good Rhone vintage is laid down in this city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cellared' is apt for wine: the good little number is laid down inside the French word. The definition 'here' works because the city sits in Rhone wine country.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is the papal city on the Rhone, right in Cotes-du-Rhone country, so it is the place meant by the question.

clue.text: Snare has component with handle that won't stop turning

indicators.note: turning says the whole string built from component and handle is read in reverse

parts.note: a part is a component

indicators.note: a word that won't stop runs on without its final letter

parts.note: handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A trap is made with a part fitted to a crank handle that keeps on rotating.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME loses its last letter ('won't stop') to give NAM; PART + NAM is then read backwards ('turning').
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a hidden device for catching trespassers, a kind of snare.

clue.text: Appeal to Liberal, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: to draw is to attract, so draw is appeal

explanation.surface: Someone makes an appeal to a Liberal voter, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like an idiom meaning 'so to speak', but 'a manner of speaking' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, drawn-out way of talking.

clue.text: Check made by tutor during break

indicators.note: during says one word comes within the time of another, so the tutor word goes inside the break word

parts.note: a rest is a break
to tutor is to train

explanation.surface: A test paper is set by a teacher in the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is a check on behaviour, holding something back.

clue.text: Cheers top player, almost out early, surprisingly

indicators.note: almost says the word for top player falls just short, losing its end

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

indicators.note: surprisingly says the following letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A top tennis player cheers, having been knocked out early to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED loses its last letter to give SEE; 'surprisingly' rearranges OUT EARLY into YOU LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is a casual British goodbye, as is the parting phrase meaning goodbye for now.

clue.text: Woman moaned regularly

indicators.note: regularly says to take letters at a steady interval, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A woman kept complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae is a woman's first name, as in Mae West.

clue.text: Several weeks stuck on mountains I'm climbing, lost

indicators.note: climbing in a down answer means going upwards, so the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: DEC, December, is a month, a span of several weeks
the Alps are mountains
I'm gives the letters I and M

explanation.surface: Someone spent weeks stranded on mountain peaks and got lost.
explanation.walkthrough: DEC + ALPS + IM, read upwards ('climbing'), gives MI SPLA CED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misplaced is put in the wrong place and so lost.

clue.text: Dog given tail of fish you caught

parts.note: bass is a fish

indicators.note: caught says the old word for you is held inside the word for tail

parts.note: the end is the tail
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A dog is given the tail end of a fish that you landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail of fish' reads as one thing, but 'tail' is its own piece and 'fish' another, joined in the other order; 'caught' holds the old word for you inside the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset hound is a breed of short-legged dog.

clue.text: Soldiers landed within Italy's frontiers, showing warlike attitude

parts.note: a host is an army, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: within says the word for landed goes inside the border letters
a country's frontiers are its edges, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: to light upon something is to land, so lit means landed

explanation.surface: Troops come ashore inside Italian borders in an aggressive mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frontiers' gives the two border letters of Italy, and 'within' puts the landed word between them; 'showing' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility is enmity, an attitude of aggression or war.

clue.text: Photograph fearsome women in bloomers

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph
dragons is slang for fierce, formidable women

explanation.surface: Someone takes a picture of formidable ladies wearing old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like baggy underwear but means flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Snapdragons are garden flowers, and bloomers is a whimsical word for plants that flower.

clue.text: More relaxed after heading off, I'll reach a Spanish resort

indicators.note: after heading off says the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: calmer means more relaxed
I'll gives the letter I, with 'will reach' read as the joining

explanation.surface: Someone, feeling calmer now, plans to get to a resort in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after heading off' removes the first letter of the relaxed word; 'I'll reach a' is read as I will join A, with 'will reach' as joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Almeria is a port and holiday resort in Andalucia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Hear shot

definitions.meaning: to hear a case in court
to have a shot at something is to have a go at it

explanation.definitionFit: Try means both to judge a case in court and an attempt, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Artist's link with explorer

parts.note: a tie is a link
Marco Polo was a Venetian explorer

explanation.surface: A painter has a connection with a famous traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' is read as 'Artist has', so 's is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an Italian painter.

clue.text: Lights a source of torment for sea creature

parts.note: lamps are lights
hell is anything that torments

explanation.surface: Bright lights are a torture for some marine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshell is a brachiopod, a shelled marine animal.

clue.text: Change dress

definitions.meaning: to change something is to move or alter it
a loose straight dress is called by the same name as a work period

explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a change, and also a simple loose-fitting dress.

clue.text: That is part of bride's trousseau

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something is said to belong in a bride's collection of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is the link between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is Latin for 'that is', usually shortened to i.e.

clue.text: Russian fighters twice meeting resistance

indicators.note: twice says the word for fighters appears two times over

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is the British reserve army
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Russian soldiers come up against opposition twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars are a Turkic people of Russia, so a Tatar is a Russian.

clue.text: Complaining vehicle has a metallic sound

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a ping is a sharp ringing sound, as of metal struck

explanation.surface: A grumbling car makes a tinny noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping means finding fault, constantly complaining.

clue.text: Doctor binds a fracture

indicators.note: binds says the doctor letters wrap around the other letter like a bandage

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor bandages a broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fracture' looks like a broken bone but means a crack or break.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a break or crack, which is a gap.

clue.text: Stop working, currently wanting holiday abroad

parts.note: a trip is a short holiday
out means away from home or overseas

explanation.surface: Someone quits their job and longs for a holiday overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' means 'in electric current terms', so the definition is a circuit breaker cutting out; 'wanting' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical equipment that trips out switches itself off, so the phrase means stop working where current flows.

clue.text: A good deal resting on launch of Daily Sketch

indicators.note: the launch of something is its start, so take the first letter

parts.note: a raft of things is a good deal of them

explanation.surface: A big contract sits on the launch of a daily newspaper's comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resting on' puts RAFT after D in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a rough first version, a sketch of something.

clue.text: One who celebrates distribution of gay report

indicators.note: distribution of says the letters are dealt out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A partygoer hands out a cheerful report.
explanation.definitionFit: A partygoer is someone who goes to parties, a reveller.
